## Correction to the Research Premise

Massachusetts town-level vital recording was ordered as early as **1639** — each town's own clerk held the original register. What began in **1841** was a *statewide, centralized* compilation layered on top of that existing system. So the town clerk's own record books are still a first-line civil source for 1820–1850, not an after-1841-only resource. Church registers and cemetery inscriptions remain essential supplementary and confirming sources — especially before 1841 and wherever a town's clerk records are incomplete — but they are not the *only* coverage for this period.

---

What began in 1841 was a *statewide, centralized* compilation layered on top of the existing town system (with Boston's records not folded in until 1850) — it did not create civil registration where none existed before. So the claim that "nothing civil exists for these years" does not hold: town clerk vital records are the first-line civil source for 1820-1850 Berkshire County, not a later-only resource. This is reinforced by `volume_search`, which found a digitized image group of "Town Clerk Vital and Town Records" for Berkshire County spanning 1761-1850 (imageGroupNumber 004500891, 512 images, 0% indexed, not full-text searchable — browse-only). Church registers and cemetery inscriptions remain essential supplementary/confirming sources, especially before any given town's clerk records survive intact or where a family's denomination recorded events the town clerk missed, but they are not the *only* record set covering the period.

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Religious denominations:** Congregational church presence confirmed in Pittsfield (Berkshire's county seat) via `volume_search` coverage (see below); other denominations not confirmed by tool results in this survey.

## Boundary changes
No boundary change for Berkshire County during 1820-1850 was returned by any tool in this survey; `place_search` shows a single continuous dateRange from 1761. ### Vital records (civil registration — town level)

- **Pre-registration alternative:** Church registers and cemetery inscriptions, detailed below, especially useful since the 1841 statewide system postdates most of this period.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Congregational, confirmed for Pittsfield, Berkshire County (county seat) via `volume_search`.

Report as a coverage gap in the indexes queried, not evidence land records don't exist — county registries of deeds are the standard Massachusetts holder.

This survey named no physical repository for Berkshire County — `catalog_search` returned zero hits for the county, which is a cataloguing gap in the FamilySearch Catalog for this place, not evidence the originals do not survive. Original town clerk vital records and church registers are customarily held by the town clerk's office and the individual congregation/diocese respectively, but no tool result in this survey named a specific office.

## Records NOT online
The two Berkshire-area image groups identified (town clerk vital/town records, and Pittsfield Congregational church records) are digitized but not name-indexed and not full-text searchable — they exist online as images only and must be browsed page by page with no name search. No Berkshire-specific land, tax, cemetery-sexton, or military collection was returned online by any tool in this survey; where these exist they appear to be physical-repository or undigitized holdings at this time.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey stated that any specific Berkshire County vital, church, or cemetery record set was destroyed or lost. Absence of an online match (e.g., zero `catalog_search` hits) is reported above as a coverage/cataloguing gap, not a loss.

## Research tips
- Town-level vital recording in Massachusetts was ordered as early as 1639, and the "original record still is found with the clerk of the town or city" — per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records — so always start with the town clerk record for the specific town, not the 1841 statewide system, for events before that date.
- The statewide centralized system began in 1841 "but not marriage intentions," and Boston's records did not appear in the state system until 1850 — a reminder that even after 1841 a town's own marriage-intention book is a distinct, separately-filed series (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records).
- Marriage intentions were "commonly recorded in the bride's home town," with additional recordings possibly in the groom's home town and their town of current residence — check all three towns for a marriage, per the same page.
- Because the family's town sits near both the New York and Vermont lines, search adjoining New York and Vermont town/county records as well as Berkshire's — a border family plausibly generated church, land, or burial records on either side; this survey did not have a town name to look up a specific Neighboring Counties table, so no adjoining counties are named here.
- Browse the two identified image groups (Berkshire town clerk/town records 1761-1850, and Pittsfield Congregational church records 1791-1850) directly by image, since neither is name-indexed.
- Treat church registers and cemetery inscriptions as primary, not merely supplementary, for any event before 1841, given the absence of a statewide civil system before that date.

---
This survey covered Berkshire County, Massachusetts for 1820 to 1850, for a family near where Massachusetts meets both New York and Vermont. The records most likely to help are local church registers (a Congregational church record set survives for the county seat, Pittsfield) and cemetery inscriptions, since Massachusetts did not centralize birth, marriage, and death records at the state level until 1841; however, each town also kept its own vital records locally going back to the 1600s, so the town clerk's own old record book is still worth checking even for these earlier years, and it survives for the county in a digitized but unindexed image set that must be looked through page by page rather than searched by name. Because the family's town is right on the New York and Vermont borders, records may also sit across the state line, and several of the specific details this survey wanted — population figures, a named cemetery, and a specific physical archive address — could not be confirmed with the tools used.

**General note (from the FamilySearch Wiki):** "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers." Even where baptism/marriage registers survive, do not expect Presbyterian burial entries. The Wiki also recommends searching Church of Ireland registers for a Presbyterian family, as some events were occasionally recorded there too.

## Census Records

Ireland's 19th-century censuses (1821–1851) were largely destroyed; the 1861 and 1871 originals were destroyed by government order. No Billy-parish census returns survive for usable family-level research.

**Substitutes:**
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s):** named directly on the Billy civil parish Wiki page — the best tool for placing the family on a specific townland close to your ancestor's 1825 birth.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: County Cork, Ireland (1830s–1840s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Munster, Ireland
- **County seat:** Cork City
- **Key context:** The Great Famine began in 1845, at the tail end of this period, and triggered mass emigration from Cork's ports — this shapes both which records survive and why the ancestor emigrated.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **State registration did not begin until 1 January 1864** for births, deaths, and Catholic marriages; non-Catholic (mainly Church of Ireland) marriages were registered from 1845.
- **There are no civil vital records for the 1830s–1840s.** Go to church records instead.

### Church Records
- **Denominations:** Roman Catholic (majority) and Church of Ireland (Anglican minority).
- Many Cork Catholic parish registers begin in the 1810s–1830s, though survival varies widely by parish.
- **Record types:** Catholic registers cover baptisms and marriages; burials are rarely recorded. Church of Ireland registers cover baptisms, marriages, and burials.
- **Where held:** The National Library of Ireland holds free online digital images of Catholic parish registers up to 1880. Church of Ireland registers are held by the Representative Church Body Library and in local custody.
- **Important:** Treat the **parish**, not the civil county, as the record-holding unit. Identify which specific Cork parish served the ancestor's townland before searching register by register.

### Census Substitutes
No usable 1841 or earlier census survives — most pre-1901 Irish census returns were destroyed in the **1922 Four Courts fire** in Dublin. Two key substitutes exist:

| Substitute | Dates | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books** | 1823–1837 | Lists occupiers of tithe-liable land — your closest "1830s census" |
| **Griffith's Valuation** | Early 1850s for Cork | Lists every householder — substitute for the destroyed 1841/1851 censuses |

### Immigration / Emigration Records
- **Port:** Cobh (then called Queenstown), Cork's main emigration port.
- Famine-era passenger manifests from Cork ports list **complete family groups, including infants and young children** traveling with parents — read the full manifest, not just the head of household.

### Land Records
Beyond the Tithe Applotment Books noted above, specific Cork land or deeds holdings were not confirmed by this survey.

### Probate, Court, Military, Cemetery, Newspaper Records
Survival and access for these in Cork in this period was not confirmed by this survey. The 1922 Four Courts fire destroyed many wills and government records nationally.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| National Library of Ireland | Free online Catholic parish register images to 1880 |
| Representative Church Body Library | Church of Ireland registers |
| Local parish custody | Some registers remain in parish hands |

> **Note:** Online catalog lookups for Cork/Ireland-specific collections and volumes could not return results in this survey run — this is a coverage gap in the indexes checked, not evidence the records don't exist. A hands-on search directly in the **FamilySearch Catalog** and the **National Library of Ireland's own parish-register website** is strongly recommended as a next step.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Go straight to Catholic parish registers** for the 1830s–1840s — there are no civil records until 1864.
2. **Use the Tithe Applotment Books** (1823–1837) as your closest 1830s "census" substitute.
3. **Use Griffith's Valuation** (Cork, early 1850s) to locate the family shortly before or after emigration, or for relatives who stayed behind.
4. **Read every line** of Famine-era passenger manifests from Cork ports — children and infants traveling with parents are listed individually.
5. **Know your townland.** The parish, not the county, is the key unit for record-finding — identify the specific parish serving your ancestor's townland before searching.
6. **Account for the 1922 fire** — wills and many government records were destroyed; adjust expectations accordingly.

---

*Source: FamilySearch Wiki, "Ireland Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy (retrieved this session).*

## Jurisdiction overview

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** None in the 1830s–1840s. Per the FamilySearch Wiki ("Ireland Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy), state registration of births and deaths, and of Roman Catholic marriages, did not begin until 1 January 1864; non-Catholic (mainly Church of Ireland) marriages were registered from 1845. There is no county-courthouse vital-records system as in the US.
- **What exists:** Nothing civil for this period — the ancestor's birth, baptism, and any marriage in the 1830s–1840s will not appear in a civil register.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church (parish) registers — see below.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (majority) and Church of Ireland (Anglican minority); per the same Wiki page, many Cork Catholic parish registers begin in the 1810s–1830s, though survival varies widely by parish.
- **Record types:** Catholic registers record baptisms and marriages; burials are rarely recorded. Church of Ireland registers record baptisms, marriages, and burials.
- **Where held:** The National Library of Ireland holds free online digital images of Catholic parish registers up to 1880 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy). Church of Ireland registers are held by the Representative Church Body Library and in local custody.
- **Gaps:** Survival varies by individual parish and was not itemized for specific Cork parishes in this run — this survey did not confirm which named Cork parishes have surviving 1830s registers; check the parish register directly.
- **Language:** Not stated on the fetched page; Catholic registers from this era are commonly in Latin, but this survey found no page confirming that for Cork specifically.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** No usable 1841 or earlier census survives — per the Wiki page, most pre-1901 Irish census returns were destroyed in the 1922 Four Courts fire.
- **Census substitutes:** The Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) list occupiers of tithe-liable land and are a key substitute for the 1830s. Griffith's Valuation, published for Cork in the early 1850s, lists every householder and substitutes for the destroyed 1841/1851 censuses (both per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy).
- **Access:** This survey could not determine online indexing/image status for either collection — `collections_search` and `volume_search` returned no matches for Cork or Ireland in this run.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
This survey's tool calls for Cork-specific and Ireland-specific online collections (`collections_search`, `volume_search`, `catalog_search`, `external_links_search`) all returned zero matches or unresolved places. The `external_links_search` result returned was generic (US-census and general sites) and not Cork- or Ireland-specific, so it is not reported as Cork coverage here. The only grounded online source found is the National Library of Ireland's free online Catholic parish register images (through 1880), per the FamilySearch Wiki page cited above — no direct URL for that collection was returned by any tool in this run.

**Coverage of this survey:** No digitized-volume or collection data for Cork could be retrieved in this run (all relevant tools returned empty results) — this is a confirmed gap in what this survey could check, not evidence the records don't exist.

### Physical repositories
This survey named no physical repository with a tool result beyond what the Wiki page states in prose: the Representative Church Body Library (Church of Ireland registers) and local parish custody. No address, catalog entry, or access procedure was returned for either.

## Records NOT online
Civil vital records (none exist for this period). Probate and court records — survival and digitization status not confirmed. Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books — this survey could not confirm their online/indexed status for Cork specifically, though they are known national-level substitute sources per the Wiki page.

- For the 1830s–1840s, go straight to Catholic parish registers rather than civil records, since none exist until 1864 ("Ireland Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy).

- When examining Famine-era passenger manifests from Cork ports, read every line of the manifest — infants and children traveling with parents are listed individually, not just the head of household.
- Treat the parish, not the civil county, as the record-holding unit for baptisms and marriages in this period; confirm which specific Cork parish served the ancestor's townland before searching register by register.
- This survey could not reach FamilySearch's Catalog, Collections, or Volume indexes for Cork or Ireland (all returned empty), so a hands-on search directly in the FamilySearch Catalog and the National Library of Ireland's own site is recommended as a next step, rather than relying on this guide's repository list.

In that era Ireland kept no government birth, marriage or death certificates at all — those only began in 1864 — so for this period the main surviving records are the local Catholic and Church of Ireland parish registers (baptisms and marriages), plus two substitute lists, the Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation, that stand in for the regular censuses, most of which were later destroyed in a 1922 fire in Dublin; family groups leaving through Cork's ports during the Famine also show up, children included, on the ships' passenger lists. args.guideSection:
## Jurisdiction overview
- **Historic status:** Lincolnshire is a maritime county on England's east coast, standardized by FamilySearch as a top-level county with date range +1801/ (place_search); its Wikipedia summary ("Genealogical and Historical Background") notes that jurisdictions subdividing older ones and administrative structure shape where records sit.
- **Administrative subdivisions:** Lincolnshire contains 620 parishes, part of another parish, and 43 extra-parochial places, and is historically divided into three Parts — Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey — each with several wapentakes; for Parliamentary purposes it was divided into North (Lindsey) and South (Kesteven and Holland) (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy).
- **County seat:** Lincoln (per the county's registration-district listings on the same page).
- **Population during period:** place_population returned no data for "Lincolnshire, England, United Kingdom" in this survey — not confirmed by this tool.
- **Religious denominations (1851 figures, the earliest tabulated on the fetched page):** 657 Church of England places of worship, 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, 38 Independent, 22 Particular Baptist, 9 Quaker, 13 Roman Catholic, and other smaller denominations (same Lincolnshire Genealogy page, citing Imperial Gazetteer of England and Wales, 1870-72). For the 1750-1800 target window, note Church of England was the established parish-register-keeping church throughout, with Methodist and other nonconformist registers growing through the later 18th century.
- **Key historical note:** this survey did not confirm specific 1750-1800 Lincolnshire events from a tool result; the general Wikipedia genealogy background only speaks to record-keeping shaped by administrative structure in general terms.

## Boundary changes
- The FamilySearch standard place for Lincolnshire carries the date range "+1801/", indicating its current standardized form is treated as continuous from 1801; place_search_all was not separately run, and no boundary change affecting the 1750-1800 period was identified by the tools used in this survey.
- Civil Registration Districts (created only from 1837, well after the target period) are listed separately (http://www.ukbmd.org.uk/genuki/REG/lin.htm, cited on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page) and should not be confused with the ancient parish/Parts structure that existed during 1750-1800.
- No boundary change specific to 1750-1800 was found; treat the county as stable for parish-register purposes in this period, organized into the Parts of Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey.

args.guideSection:
### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National civil registration of births, marriages and deaths in England and Wales began 1 July 1837 (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration). This is after the 1750-1800 target period, so no civil vital records exist for this window.
- **What exists for 1750-1800:** None at the civil level — see Church records below for the operative record type.
- **Where held:** N/A for this period.
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Church of England parish registers (baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials), held at the parish level; see Church records.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England was the established, parish-register-keeping church; nonconformist groups (Methodist, Baptist, Quaker, Independent, Roman Catholic) were present but their 1851 totals (657 C of E vs. 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, etc.) are from a later tabulation (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy) — nonconformist registers for 1750-1800 would be thinner than these later figures suggest.
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages (banns and licence), burials, kept by the parish.
- **Indexed options found:** England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975 at FamilySearch (collection 1473014) and England Marriages, 1538-1973 (collection 1473015) — both are indexes covering the target period, but the Births/Christenings collection is explicitly flagged a Legacy collection (see quirks) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records). Great Britain, Births and Baptisms, 1571-1977 (collection 1770884) is also an index, "incomplete" per the wiki page.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexes above); Ancestry's England & Wales, Christening Index 1530-1980 and England & Wales Marriages 1538-1988 (subscription); Findmypast's Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 and Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837 (both named in external_links_search results, subscription). volume_search found 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes overlapping 1750-1800, the large majority browse-only images of original parish registers (see Repository guide).
- **Gaps:** This survey did not confirm destroyed Lincolnshire parish registers for 1750-1800 from any tool result — absence of an indexed hit is a coverage/indexing gap, not evidence of loss.
- **Language:** English (confirmed by volume_search's `languages: ["en"]` on the Lincolnshire volumes examined).

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** The first UK census was 1841 (per catalog_search hits for Lincolnshire 1841/1851/1871/1881/1891 census surname indexes); no census exists for 1750-1800.
- **State/provincial census:** Not applicable/none found for this period.
- **Other enumerations:** Lincolnshire Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861 and Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860 (Findmypast, via external_links_search) and Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865 fall inside the target window and can substitute for population enumeration by documenting where people were settled or removed.
- **Access:** 1841-1891 census surname indexes are catalog/fiche-based finding aids (e.g. koha:697142, koha:688165, koha:676270) at the FamilySearch Library, not online name-search for the 1750-1800 period itself.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations — England & Wales, Prerogative Court of Canterbury (PCC) Wills, 1384-1858 and its Index of Will Registers (via external_links_search, Ancestry/MyHeritage); Bank Of England Wills Extracts 1717-1845; England & Wales Published Wills & Probate Indexes, 1300-1858 (Findmypast).
- **Testate or intestate:** Search the will series (PCC or lower consistory/archdeaconry courts) if testate; the equivalent administration bonds/grants if intestate — this survey did not retrieve the specific Lincolnshire archdeaconry/consistory court names, so consult Lincolnshire Archives directly for pre-1858 lower probate jurisdiction records.
- **Date range:** PCC Wills run 1384-1858, covering the full target period.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch/Ancestry/MyHeritage indexes (subscription for most); original Lincolnshire lower-court probate records would be at Lincolnshire Archives (http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx, named on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page) — this survey found no tool result confirming the exact pre-1858 probate jurisdiction structure for Lincolnshire parishes.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by any tool result in this survey (England generally used deeds/manorial records rather than the US rectangular survey system; not parish-specific here).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed — no `{Jurisdiction}_Land_and_Property` page for Lincolnshire specifically was fetched in this survey; England, Return of Owners of Land, 1873 (Ancestry, via external_links_search) postdates the target period.
- **Types:** Manorial records (Manorial Documents Register, The National Archives, index only, linked from England Online Genealogy Records) are the main land/tenure record type reaching back into this period for English villages.
- **Date range/held:** Manorial Documents Register is an index only (no images); consult The National Archives directly (https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/manor-search).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The target window includes the Seven Years' War (1756-1763), the American War of Independence (1775-1783), and the early French Revolutionary Wars (from 1793).
- **Record types:** UK, Royal Hospital Chelsea Pensioner Registers of Soldiers Who Served in Canada, 1743-1882 and Chelsea Pensioners' Service Records, 1760-1913 (FamilySearch collection 1952868) both overlap the period; British Royal Navy Ships' Musters, 1739-1861 (FamilySearch collection 4231104, 279,822 people) covers naval service throughout 1750-1800.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexed, collections above); Ancestry/Findmypast (subscription) for officer and pension records.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not named by any tool result for Lincolnshire specifically in this survey.
- **Online coverage:** Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s and National Burial Index for England & Wales (both via Findmypast, external_links_search); England BillionGraves Cemetery Index; FindAGrave (general, not Lincolnshire-specific confirmed).
- **Physical records:** Parish burial registers (see Church records) are the primary 1750-1800 cemetery source — monumental inscriptions from this early period are comparatively sparse since durable gravestones for ordinary parishioners became common only later.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not named by any tool result in this survey.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (http://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/, external_links_search) is the general finding aid named for England; no Lincolnshire-specific 18th-century title was confirmed.
- **Content value:** Marriage/death notices for the gentry are more likely than for ordinary parishioners in this period.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Boston, Lincolnshire was a historic port; this survey did not confirm a specific emigration record set naming it.
- **Record types:** A List of Emigrants from England to America, 1682-1692, 1718-1759 and Emigrants in Bondage, 1614-1775 (Ancestry, external_links_search) both overlap part of the target window.
- **Where held:** Ancestry (subscription).
- **Content note:** examine full passenger/emigrant lists for all family members, including children, when such lists are located.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poll tax, settlement-related records.
- **Date range:** The 1641 Lincolnshire poll tax returns (catalog_search koha:688213, Lincolnshire Family History Society) predate the period; Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860 and Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861 (Findmypast) substitute for tax/residency documentation across 1750-1800.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (fiche, per filmNotes on koha:688213); Findmypast (subscription, online).
- **Substitute value:** Settlement examinations/certificates and poor law removal records (Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865) can substitute for missing census-era population data, since no census existed before 1841.

### Other record types
- Lincolnshire Parish Apprentice Index, 1618-1925 and Lincolnshire Parish Bastardy Cases (Findmypast, external_links_search) both reach into the target period and name individuals not found in baptism/marriage/burial registers alone.

args.guideSection:
## Research tips
- Church records are the only source for pre-1837 births, marriages and deaths in England — "Before 1837 only churches recorded birth, marriage, and death information" (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration).
- Search indexed FamilySearch collections first (England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975; England Marriages, 1538-1973) but verify every Legacy-collection hit against the original register, since that collection "is a partial index...no additional records will be added, or any corrections made" (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
- Because most of the 1,066 Lincolnshire parish-register volumes found for 1750-1800 are browse-only images (not name-indexed), plan to browse individual parish registers image-by-image once the specific parish of interest is known, rather than relying solely on index search.
- Lincolnshire is organized into the three historic Parts (Holland, Kesteven, Lindsey) and many finding aids (e.g. census surname indexes) are arranged by 19th-century civil registration district — know which registration district/Part a parish fell in before searching county-level finding aids (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy).
- Follow England's general research sequence: identify what you know, document sources, set a specific goal, then select records to search using the England Record Finder (FamilySearch Wiki, England Getting Started: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Getting_Started).
- For marriages after 1837 only, there is no need to order a civil certificate since the church register is an exact duplicate — not relevant to the 1750-1800 window itself, but useful if following the same family forward (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration).

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975 (collection 1473014); England Marriages, 1538-1973 (collection 1473015); Great Britain, Births and Baptisms, 1571-1977 (collection 1770884, "incomplete") | indexed baptism/christening and marriage search spanning 1750-1800 | not stated |
| Ancestry | England & Wales, Christening Index, 1530-1980; England & Wales Marriages, 1538-1988; Lincolnshire, England Extracted Church of England Parish Records, 1500s-1800s | indexed baptism/marriage search; Lincolnshire-specific extracted parish records | subscription ($) |
| Findmypast | Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 (browse); Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837; Lincolnshire Baptisms; Lincolnshire Burials | Lincolnshire-specific indexed/browse parish register access for the full target period | subscription ($) |
| joinermarriageindex.co.uk | Joiner's Marriage Index, 110 Lincolnshire parishes indexed | free regional marriage index covering many Lincolnshire parishes | not stated |
| FreeReg | volunteer transcriptions of parish registers | free alternative to subscription parish-register indexes | free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes matched 1750-1800 in volume_search; only the first 10 were examined in detail above (a `nextPageToken` was returned), so most of the matched set was not individually reviewed. catalog_search returned 5,444 total hits for Lincolnshire, of which only the first 25 (10 hydrated with full detail) were examined.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Lincolnshire Archives | County archive named on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page as the county repository (http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx); likely custodian of original parish registers and probate records, though no catalog_search hit in this survey explicitly confirmed it as the originals' holder | online catalogue; visit or write for originals |
| FamilySearch Library | Microfilm/fiche copies of Lincolnshire census surname indexes, poll tax indexes, and marriage licence abstracts (per catalog_search filmNotes, e.g. koha:688213, koha:688165) | visit a FamilySearch Center or affiliate library |

## Records NOT online
- The great majority of Lincolnshire's digitized 1750-1800 parish-register images (Vital 375 of 380, Baptism 645 of 650, Religious Death 434 of 434, Religious Marriage 519 of 519 browse-only per volume_search summary) exist only as browse-only scanned images, not as name-searchable online records.
- Pre-1858 lower ecclesiastical-court probate records (below the Prerogative Court of Canterbury) were not located online in this survey; Lincolnshire Archives should be consulted directly.
- Manorial records for Lincolnshire parishes are indexed only in The National Archives' Manorial Documents Register, with no online images found.

## Known record losses
- No tool result in this survey stated that Lincolnshire parish registers for 1750-1800 were destroyed or lost. Absence of a specific collection from collections_search or volume_search is a coverage/digitization gap, not evidence of loss.

This survey looked at Lincolnshire, England between 1750 and 1800, focused on finding christenings and marriages. Next, a research plan can be built from this guide to search the indexed FamilySearch, Ancestry and Findmypast collections for the specific parishes of interest, falling back to browsing the unindexed register images where needed.

# Locality Guide: Lincolnshire, England (1750-1800)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Historic status:** Lincolnshire is a maritime county on England's east coast, standardized by FamilySearch as a top-level county with date range +1801/ (place_search); its Wikipedia summary ("Genealogical and Historical Background") notes that jurisdictions subdividing older ones and administrative structure shape where records sit.
- **Administrative subdivisions:** Lincolnshire contains 620 parishes, part of another parish, and 43 extra-parochial places, and is historically divided into three Parts — Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey — each with several wapentakes; for Parliamentary purposes it was divided into North (Lindsey) and South (Kesteven and Holland) (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy).
- **County seat:** Lincoln (per the county's registration-district listings on the same page).
- **Population during period:** place_population returned no data for "Lincolnshire, England, United Kingdom" in this survey — not confirmed by this tool.
- **Religious denominations (1851 figures, the earliest tabulated on the fetched page):** 657 Church of England places of worship, 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, 38 Independent, 22 Particular Baptist, 9 Quaker, 13 Roman Catholic, and other smaller denominations (same Lincolnshire Genealogy page, citing Imperial Gazetteer of England and Wales, 1870-72). For the 1750-1800 target window, note Church of England was the established parish-register-keeping church throughout, with Methodist and other nonconformist registers growing through the later 18th century.
- **Key historical note:** this survey did not confirm specific 1750-1800 Lincolnshire events from a tool result; the general Wikipedia genealogy background only speaks to record-keeping shaped by administrative structure in general terms.

## Boundary changes
- The FamilySearch standard place for Lincolnshire carries the date range "+1801/", indicating its current standardized form is treated as continuous from 1801; place_search_all was not separately run, and no boundary change affecting the 1750-1800 period was identified by the tools used in this survey.
- Civil Registration Districts (created only from 1837, well after the target period) are listed separately (http://www.ukbmd.org.uk/genuki/REG/lin.htm, cited on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page) and should not be confused with the ancient parish/Parts structure that existed during 1750-1800.
- No boundary change specific to 1750-1800 was found; treat the county as stable for parish-register purposes in this period, organized into the Parts of Holland, Kesteven, and Lindsey.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National civil registration of births, marriages and deaths in England and Wales began 1 July 1837 (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration). This is after the 1750-1800 target period, so no civil vital records exist for this window.
- **What exists for 1750-1800:** None at the civil level — see Church records below for the operative record type.
- **Where held:** N/A for this period.
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Church of England parish registers (baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials), held at the parish level; see Church records.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England was the established, parish-register-keeping church; nonconformist groups (Methodist, Baptist, Quaker, Independent, Roman Catholic) were present but their 1851 totals (657 C of E vs. 462 Wesleyan Methodist, 221 Primitive Methodist, etc.) are from a later tabulation (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy) — nonconformist registers for 1750-1800 would be thinner than these later figures suggest.
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages (banns and licence), burials, kept by the parish.
- **Indexed options found:** England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975 at FamilySearch (collection 1473014) and England Marriages, 1538-1973 (collection 1473015) — both are indexes covering the target period, but the Births/Christenings collection is explicitly flagged a Legacy collection (see quirks) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records). Great Britain, Births and Baptisms, 1571-1977 (collection 1770884) is also an index, "incomplete" per the wiki page.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexes above); Ancestry's England & Wales, Christening Index 1530-1980 and England & Wales Marriages 1538-1988 (subscription); Findmypast's Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 and Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837 (both named in external_links_search results, subscription). volume_search found 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes overlapping 1750-1800, the large majority browse-only images of original parish registers (see Repository guide).
- **Gaps:** This survey did not confirm destroyed Lincolnshire parish registers for 1750-1800 from any tool result — absence of an indexed hit is a coverage/indexing gap, not evidence of loss.
- **Language:** English (confirmed by volume_search's `languages: ["en"]` on the Lincolnshire volumes examined).

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** The first UK census was 1841 (per catalog_search hits for Lincolnshire 1841/1851/1871/1881/1891 census surname indexes); no census exists for 1750-1800.
- **State/provincial census:** Not applicable/none found for this period.
- **Other enumerations:** Lincolnshire Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861 and Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860 (Findmypast, via external_links_search) and Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865 fall inside the target window and can substitute for population enumeration by documenting where people were settled or removed.
- **Access:** 1841-1891 census surname indexes are catalog/fiche-based finding aids (e.g. koha:697142, koha:688165, koha:676270) at the FamilySearch Library, not online name-search for the 1750-1800 period itself.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations — England & Wales, Prerogative Court of Canterbury (PCC) Wills, 1384-1858 and its Index of Will Registers (via external_links_search, Ancestry/MyHeritage); Bank Of England Wills Extracts 1717-1845; England & Wales Published Wills & Probate Indexes, 1300-1858 (Findmypast).
- **Testate or intestate:** Search the will series (PCC or lower consistory/archdeaconry courts) if testate; the equivalent administration bonds/grants if intestate — this survey did not retrieve the specific Lincolnshire archdeaconry/consistory court names, so consult Lincolnshire Archives directly for pre-1858 lower probate jurisdiction records.
- **Date range:** PCC Wills run 1384-1858, covering the full target period.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch/Ancestry/MyHeritage indexes (subscription for most); original Lincolnshire lower-court probate records would be at Lincolnshire Archives (http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx, named on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page) — this survey found no tool result confirming the exact pre-1858 probate jurisdiction structure for Lincolnshire parishes.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by any tool result in this survey (England generally used deeds/manorial records rather than the US rectangular survey system; not parish-specific here).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed — no `{Jurisdiction}_Land_and_Property` page for Lincolnshire specifically was fetched in this survey; England, Return of Owners of Land, 1873 (Ancestry, via external_links_search) postdates the target period.
- **Types:** Manorial records (Manorial Documents Register, The National Archives, index only, linked from England Online Genealogy Records) are the main land/tenure record type reaching back into this period for English villages.
- **Date range/held:** Manorial Documents Register is an index only (no images); consult The National Archives directly (https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/manor-search).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The target window includes the Seven Years' War (1756-1763), the American War of Independence (1775-1783), and the early French Revolutionary Wars (from 1793).
- **Record types:** UK, Royal Hospital Chelsea Pensioner Registers of Soldiers Who Served in Canada, 1743-1882 and Chelsea Pensioners' Service Records, 1760-1913 (FamilySearch collection 1952868) both overlap the period; British Royal Navy Ships' Musters, 1739-1861 (FamilySearch collection 4231104, 279,822 people) covers naval service throughout 1750-1800.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexed, collections above); Ancestry/Findmypast (subscription) for officer and pension records.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not named by any tool result for Lincolnshire specifically in this survey.
- **Online coverage:** Lincolnshire Monumental Inscriptions, 1400s-2000s and National Burial Index for England & Wales (both via Findmypast, external_links_search); England BillionGraves Cemetery Index; FindAGrave (general, not Lincolnshire-specific confirmed).
- **Physical records:** Parish burial registers (see Church records) are the primary 1750-1800 cemetery source — monumental inscriptions from this early period are comparatively sparse since durable gravestones for ordinary parishioners became common only later.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not named by any tool result in this survey.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (http://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/, external_links_search) is the general finding aid named for England; no Lincolnshire-specific 18th-century title was confirmed.
- **Content value:** Marriage/death notices for the gentry are more likely than for ordinary parishioners in this period.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Boston, Lincolnshire was a historic port; this survey did not confirm a specific emigration record set naming it.
- **Record types:** A List of Emigrants from England to America, 1682-1692, 1718-1759 and Emigrants in Bondage, 1614-1775 (Ancestry, external_links_search) both overlap part of the target window.
- **Where held:** Ancestry (subscription).
- **Content note:** examine full passenger/emigrant lists for all family members, including children, when such lists are located.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Poll tax, settlement-related records.
- **Date range:** The 1641 Lincolnshire poll tax returns (catalog_search koha:688213, Lincolnshire Family History Society) predate the period; Lincolnshire Settlement Certificates, 1675-1860 and Settlement Examinations, 1721-1861 (Findmypast) substitute for tax/residency documentation across 1750-1800.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (fiche, per filmNotes on koha:688213); Findmypast (subscription, online).
- **Substitute value:** Settlement examinations/certificates and poor law removal records (Lincolnshire Poor Law Removals, 1665-1865) can substitute for missing census-era population data, since no census existed before 1841.

### Other record types
- Lincolnshire Parish Apprentice Index, 1618-1925 and Lincolnshire Parish Bastardy Cases (Findmypast, external_links_search) both reach into the target period and name individuals not found in baptism/marriage/burial registers alone.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975 (collection 1473014); England Marriages, 1538-1973 (collection 1473015); Great Britain, Births and Baptisms, 1571-1977 (collection 1770884, "incomplete") | indexed baptism/christening and marriage search spanning 1750-1800 | not stated |
| Ancestry | England & Wales, Christening Index, 1530-1980; England & Wales Marriages, 1538-1988; Lincolnshire, England Extracted Church of England Parish Records, 1500s-1800s | indexed baptism/marriage search; Lincolnshire-specific extracted parish records | subscription ($) |
| Findmypast | Lincolnshire Parish Registers, 1538-1911 (browse); Lincolnshire Marriages and Banns, 1754-1837; Lincolnshire Baptisms; Lincolnshire Burials | Lincolnshire-specific indexed/browse parish register access for the full target period | subscription ($) |
| joinermarriageindex.co.uk | Joiner's Marriage Index, 110 Lincolnshire parishes indexed | free regional marriage index covering many Lincolnshire parishes | not stated |
| FreeReg | volunteer transcriptions of parish registers | free alternative to subscription parish-register indexes | free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 1,066 digitized Lincolnshire volumes matched 1750-1800 in volume_search; only the first 10 were examined in detail above (a `nextPageToken` was returned), so most of the matched set was not individually reviewed. catalog_search returned 5,444 total hits for Lincolnshire, of which only the first 25 (10 hydrated with full detail) were examined.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Lincolnshire Archives | County archive named on the Lincolnshire Genealogy page as the county repository (http://www.calmview.eu/lincolnshirearchives/calmview/default.aspx); likely custodian of original parish registers and probate records, though no catalog_search hit in this survey explicitly confirmed it as the originals' holder | online catalogue; visit or write for originals |
| FamilySearch Library | Microfilm/fiche copies of Lincolnshire census surname indexes, poll tax indexes, and marriage licence abstracts (per catalog_search filmNotes, e.g. koha:688213, koha:688165) | visit a FamilySearch Center or affiliate library |

## Records NOT online
- The great majority of Lincolnshire's digitized 1750-1800 parish-register images (Vital 375 of 380, Baptism 645 of 650, Religious Death 434 of 434, Religious Marriage 519 of 519 browse-only per volume_search summary) exist only as browse-only scanned images, not as name-searchable online records.
- Pre-1858 lower ecclesiastical-court probate records (below the Prerogative Court of Canterbury) were not located online in this survey; Lincolnshire Archives should be consulted directly.
- Manorial records for Lincolnshire parishes are indexed only in The National Archives' Manorial Documents Register, with no online images found.

## Known record losses
- No tool result in this survey stated that Lincolnshire parish registers for 1750-1800 were destroyed or lost. Absence of a specific collection from collections_search or volume_search is a coverage/digitization gap, not evidence of loss.

## Research tips
- Church records are the only source for pre-1837 births, marriages and deaths in England — "Before 1837 only churches recorded birth, marriage, and death information" (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration).
- Search indexed FamilySearch collections first (England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975; England Marriages, 1538-1973) but verify every Legacy-collection hit against the original register, since that collection "is a partial index...no additional records will be added, or any corrections made" (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
- Because most of the 1,066 Lincolnshire parish-register volumes found for 1750-1800 are browse-only images (not name-indexed), plan to browse individual parish registers image-by-image once the specific parish of interest is known, rather than relying solely on index search.
- Lincolnshire is organized into the three historic Parts (Holland, Kesteven, Lindsey) and many finding aids (e.g. census surname indexes) are arranged by 19th-century civil registration district — know which registration district/Part a parish fell in before searching county-level finding aids (FamilySearch Wiki, Lincolnshire, England Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lincolnshire,_England_Genealogy).
- Follow England's general research sequence: identify what you know, document sources, set a specific goal, then select records to search using the England Record Finder (FamilySearch Wiki, England Getting Started: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Getting_Started).
- For marriages after 1837 only, there is no need to order a civil certificate since the church register is an exact duplicate — not relevant to the 1750-1800 window itself, but useful if following the same family forward (FamilySearch Wiki, England Civil Registration).

## Württemberg, Germany — Lutheran Church Books (1780–1830)

**Key findings for baptisms and marriages:**

**No civil registration in this period.** Government vital registration did not begin in Württemberg until 1876. For 1780–1830, the Lutheran *Kirchenbücher* (church books) kept by the local parish minister are the **only original records** of baptisms, marriages, and burials.

**Where the records are held:**
- **Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart** — the regional Lutheran church archive; physical repository for the original registers.
- **Archion** (archion.de) — subscription service with Württemberg church books, browsable page-by-page.
- **Ancestry** — holds some Württemberg Lutheran collections.
- **FamilySearch** — partial coverage; many volumes are digitized but not name-indexed, requiring page-by-page browsing rather than name search.

**Critical note for this family — double given names:**
- Children baptized with two given names were commonly called in daily life by the **second name**, not the first. Search under *both* names.
- If a child died young, parents frequently **reused the same pair of names** for a later child of the same sex. Always confirm deaths before assuming a named child is the right individual.

**Next steps:** Use this guide to build a research plan and execute searches in the Württemberg Lutheran collections, particularly via Archion for browsable image access to the specific parishes of interest.

args.guideSection:
## Jurisdiction overview
- **Governing jurisdiction 1780-1830:** Duchy of Württemberg (until 1803), then Electorate (1803-1806), then Kingdom of Württemberg (from 1806). FamilySearch's standard place for this era is "Württemberg" (dateRange 1495-1871), distinct from the later "Württemberg, Germany" state (1871-1945) used after German unification.
- **Capital/administrative center:** Stuttgart.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Part of the Holy Roman Empire until 1806, then a sovereign member state of the Confederation of the Rhine and later the German Confederation.
- **Population:** No Württemberg-specific figures were returned by this survey; place_population returned only country-level German estimates (about 18-28 million, 1800-1830) and country-level indexed birth-record counts (29.2 million records 1750-1800; 35.3 million 1800-1850), not Württemberg-specific figures.
- **Religion:** Predominantly Lutheran (Evangelisch), with a Catholic minority and some Reformed congregations; Catholic and Lutheran records are catalogued and held as entirely separate series (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Key period fact:** This survey found no Württemberg-specific economic/historical detail beyond what is in the jurisdiction and records sections below; the FamilySearch Wiki's Württemberg genealogy page is a thin stub that mainly maps the 1871 jurisdiction to the modern state of Baden-Württemberg (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).

args.guideSection:
## Boundary changes
- Württemberg went from Duchy to Electorate (1803) to Kingdom (1806) during this window, absorbing numerous small neighboring territories (free imperial cities, ecclesiastical territories, small counties) through German mediatization (1803-1806), which can shift which jurisdiction's archive holds a given village's earlier records.
- After German unification in 1871, the FamilySearch Catalog began organizing records by the 1871 Meyers Gazetteer place names; records from the 1780-1830 window are catalogued under those same 1871-era parish/Oberamt names, not under pre-1803 territorial names (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).
- In 1945-1951 Württemberg merged with Baden and Hohenzollern into modern Baden-Württemberg; this is a later change and does not affect record location for 1780-1830, but a modern-day archive address will be under Baden-Württemberg state archives.

args.guideSection:
### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Statewide civil registration of births, marriages and deaths did not begin in Württemberg until 1 January 1876, well after the 1780-1830 target window (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration). Württemberg was east of the Rhine and was not among the areas (Rheinland, parts of Hessen, Alsace-Lorraine, etc.) where Napoleonic-era civil registration (1792-1815) was introduced.
- **What exists for 1780-1830:** No civil vital records for this period and place; church registers are the primary record for births/baptisms, marriages, and deaths/burials.
- **Where held:** Not applicable for this period (post-1876 civil records are held locally at each Standesamt or in state archives per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration).
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Lutheran (and Catholic) parish church books are the controlling record type for this entire window; see Church records below.

args.guideSection:
### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran (Evangelisch) churches began requiring baptism/marriage/burial records around 1540; Catholic parish records were mandated from 1563 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Württemberg is predominantly Lutheran.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (Taufen), marriages (Heiraten) including banns/proclamations (Aufgebote), burials (Begräbnisse), and confirmations (Konfirmationen, usually age ~14 for Protestants). Württemberg and Baden parishes are specifically noted (post-1808) for keeping Family Registers (Familienbücher) consolidating a family's births, marriage, and deaths on one page.
- **Two-given-names note:** Baptism registers record the infant's full name as given (often 2+ given names); which one the child was actually called by varied by locality/era and was often the second name, so cross-check later records (marriage, confirmation, burial) under any of the recorded given names (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Naming_Customs).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Historical Records collection "Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971" (id 3015626, 212,026,468 persons, covers 1499-1971) and "Germany, Württemberg, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1818-1915" (id 4132030, 64,917 persons) via collections_search. The Württemberg Evangelical regional church's own records are held at the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart, reachable online (subscription) via Archion, and also via Ancestry's "Württemberg, Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1985" (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Gaps:** This survey found no record-destruction statement specific to Württemberg; the FamilySearch Wiki names only general German losses (Thirty Years' War destruction pre-1650; WWII losses mainly in areas now Poland), neither applicable to this place/period as stated by a tool result.
- **Language:** Protestant registers in this period and place are generally in German; Catholic registers were usually in Latin until the 1800s (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Expect German old-script (Kurrent/Sütterlin) handwriting.

args.guideSection:
### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Court/probate-adjacent records in this German-village context are usually property-transfer and tax records (Schuld- und Pfandprotokolle, Steuerlisten/Steuerrollen) rather than Anglo-American wills; about 90% of the Württemberg-era rural population held land by usufruct, not ownership, and such transactions were recorded in court/administrative registers (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Testate or intestate:** Not determined by this survey; collections_search returned one relevant item, "Germany, Württemberg, Schwäbisch Hall, Probate Records, 1803-1929" (id 1475994), which overlaps the tail of this period for that locality only.
- **Date range:** 1803-1929 for the Schwäbisch Hall collection found; no broader Württemberg probate collection was found by this survey.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog/local courthouse (Amtsgericht) equivalents; the Schwäbisch Hall collection is indexed per collections_search but its online/browse status was not separately confirmed here.

- **Types:** Steuerlisten/Steuerrollen (tax lists) and Amtsrechnungen (administrative accounts), paid twice yearly; used by researchers to track household heads and widow/remarriage transitions (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).

- **Confirmation records (Konfirmationen):** 1,065 volumes matched by volume_search for this place/period, 493 browse-only; a useful supplement when baptism entries are missing or ambiguous between same-named siblings.
- **Genealogies/compiled lineage books:** 189 "Genealogies" group volumes matched (175 browse-only), including local Ortssippenbücher (parish lineage books) and town histories (e.g. catalog_search hits like "1000 Jahre Heutingsheim" and similar Jahre-titled local histories) that sometimes reprint or index early church-book entries no longer legible in the originals.
- **Government/administrative records:** 1,304 volumes matched (705 browse-only) in that group for this place/period.

args.guideSection:
## Research tips
- Almost all German research for this period rests on two record types: church records and (once it begins, 1876) civil registration — for 1780-1830 that means church records alone (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).

# Locality Guide: Württemberg, Germany (Lutheran church-book baptisms and marriages) (1780-1830)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Governing jurisdiction 1780-1830:** Duchy of Württemberg (until 1803), then Electorate (1803-1806), then Kingdom of Württemberg (from 1806). FamilySearch's standard place for this era is "Württemberg" (dateRange 1495-1871), distinct from the later "Württemberg, Germany" state (1871-1945) used after German unification.
- **Capital/administrative center:** Stuttgart.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Part of the Holy Roman Empire until 1806, then a sovereign member state of the Confederation of the Rhine and later the German Confederation.
- **Population:** No Württemberg-specific figures were returned by this survey; place_population returned only country-level German estimates (about 18-28 million, 1800-1830) and country-level indexed birth-record counts (29.2 million records 1750-1800; 35.3 million 1800-1850), not Württemberg-specific figures.
- **Religion:** Predominantly Lutheran (Evangelisch), with a Catholic minority and some Reformed congregations; Catholic and Lutheran records are catalogued and held as entirely separate series (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Key period fact:** This survey found no Württemberg-specific economic/historical detail beyond what is in the jurisdiction and records sections below; the FamilySearch Wiki's Württemberg genealogy page is a thin stub that mainly maps the 1871 jurisdiction to the modern state of Baden-Württemberg (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).

## Boundary changes
- Württemberg went from Duchy to Electorate (1803) to Kingdom (1806) during this window, absorbing numerous small neighboring territories (free imperial cities, ecclesiastical territories, small counties) through German mediatization (1803-1806), which can shift which jurisdiction's archive holds a given village's earlier records.
- After German unification in 1871, the FamilySearch Catalog began organizing records by the 1871 Meyers Gazetteer place names; records from the 1780-1830 window are catalogued under those same 1871-era parish/Oberamt names, not under pre-1803 territorial names (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/W%C3%BCrttemberg,_Germany_Genealogy).
- In 1945-1951 Württemberg merged with Baden and Hohenzollern into modern Baden-Württemberg; this is a later change and does not affect record location for 1780-1830, but a modern-day archive address will be under Baden-Württemberg state archives.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Statewide civil registration of births, marriages and deaths did not begin in Württemberg until 1 January 1876, well after the 1780-1830 target window (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration). Württemberg was east of the Rhine and was not among the areas (Rheinland, parts of Hessen, Alsace-Lorraine, etc.) where Napoleonic-era civil registration (1792-1815) was introduced.
- **What exists for 1780-1830:** No civil vital records for this period and place; church registers are the primary record for births/baptisms, marriages, and deaths/burials.
- **Where held:** Not applicable for this period (post-1876 civil records are held locally at each Standesamt or in state archives per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Civil_Registration).
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Lutheran (and Catholic) parish church books are the controlling record type for this entire window; see Church records below.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran (Evangelisch) churches began requiring baptism/marriage/burial records around 1540; Catholic parish records were mandated from 1563 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Württemberg is predominantly Lutheran.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (Taufen), marriages (Heiraten) including banns/proclamations (Aufgebote), burials (Begräbnisse), and confirmations (Konfirmationen, usually age ~14 for Protestants). Württemberg and Baden parishes are specifically noted (post-1808) for keeping Family Registers (Familienbücher) consolidating a family's births, marriage, and deaths on one page.
- **Two-given-names note:** Baptism registers record the infant's full name as given (often 2+ given names); which one the child was actually called by varied by locality/era and was often the second name, so cross-check later records (marriage, confirmation, burial) under any of the recorded given names (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Naming_Customs).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Historical Records collection "Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971" (id 3015626, 212,026,468 persons, covers 1499-1971) and "Germany, Württemberg, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1818-1915" (id 4132030, 64,917 persons) via collections_search. The Württemberg Evangelical regional church's own records are held at the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart, reachable online (subscription) via Archion, and also via Ancestry's "Württemberg, Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1985" (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records).
- **Gaps:** This survey found no record-destruction statement specific to Württemberg; the FamilySearch Wiki names only general German losses (Thirty Years' War destruction pre-1650; WWII losses mainly in areas now Poland), neither applicable to this place/period as stated by a tool result.
- **Language:** Protestant registers in this period and place are generally in German; Catholic registers were usually in Latin until the 1800s (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Church_Records). Expect German old-script (Kurrent/Sütterlin) handwriting.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** Not confirmed by this survey for the 1780-1830 window; no Württemberg-specific census collection appeared in collections_search for this period. A later "Germany, Württemberg" census series was not surfaced by the tools used in this survey.
- **State/provincial census:** This survey did not confirm any Württemberg state census for 1780-1830.
- **Other enumerations:** Family Registers (Familienbücher, post-1808) and parish lineage books (Ortssippenbücher) function as census-like family enumerations for this period and place; see Church records above.
- **Access:** Not applicable where no collection was found; treat census as a gap for this window.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Court/probate-adjacent records in this German-village context are usually property-transfer and tax records (Schuld- und Pfandprotokolle, Steuerlisten/Steuerrollen) rather than Anglo-American wills; about 90% of the Württemberg-era rural population held land by usufruct, not ownership, and such transactions were recorded in court/administrative registers (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Testate or intestate:** Not determined by this survey; collections_search returned one relevant item, "Germany, Württemberg, Schwäbisch Hall, Probate Records, 1803-1929" (id 1475994), which overlaps the tail of this period for that locality only.
- **Date range:** 1803-1929 for the Schwäbisch Hall collection found; no broader Württemberg probate collection was found by this survey.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog/local courthouse (Amtsgericht) equivalents; the Schwäbisch Hall collection is indexed per collections_search but its online/browse status was not separately confirmed here.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by this survey; no Württemberg land-survey-system detail was returned by any tool.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed; this survey did not read a Württemberg-specific Land and Property wiki page (only the general Germany_Land_and_Property topic link was surfaced, not fetched in this pass).
- **Types:** volume_search's summary lists 19 "Land" group volumes matching Württemberg for 1780-1830, all browse-only (0 fulltext/indexed).
- **Date range:** As covered by those 19 volumes; specific years not broken out in the summary.
- **Where held:** Not stated by a tool result for this place; likely local/state archives (Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg appears among external_links_search results for related church-book duplicates).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars (1792-1815) directly affected Württemberg during this window, including French occupation influence in parts of Germany (noted generally, not Württemberg-specifically, by the FamilySearch Wiki).
- **Record types:** volume_search's summary shows only 1 "Military" group volume matching Württemberg for 1780-1830 (browse-only). External collections include general "Germany & Austria, Directories of Military and Marine Officers, 1500-1939" and "Germany and Austria, Military and Marine Unit Histories, 1760-1933" (Ancestry, subscription).
- **Where held:** Not specifically stated for Württemberg by a tool result in this survey; likely state military archives.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not named by any tool result for this specific place/period.
- **Online coverage:** BillionGraves ("Cemetery Search") and Germany Find a Grave Index (Ancestry, 1600s forward, subscription) were returned by the Germany-wide online records page as general coverage; no Württemberg-specific cemetery collection was confirmed.
- **Physical records:** Burial entries for this period are recorded in the Lutheran parish burial registers (Begräbnisse) themselves; see Church records above, not a separate sexton series.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not confirmed by this survey; volume_search's summary lists 6 "Newspapers" group volumes matching Württemberg 1780-1830, all browse-only; no titles or date ranges were returned.
- **Where held:** Not stated; general German newspaper links (e.g. onlinenewspapers.com/germany.htm) appeared in external_links_search as a general, undated resource.
- **Content value:** Not applicable for this early, pre-newspaper-coverage period based on available tool data.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not inland-irrelevant: Württemberg was a major source of emigration later in the 1800s via Bremen and other ports; for 1780-1830 specifically no port-level detail was returned by any tool.
- **Record types:** External collections include "Württemberg, Germany Emigration Index, 1808-1890" (Ancestry) and "Auswanderung aus Südwestdeutschland, 1751-1920" (auswanderer-bw.de) — both overlap the tail of the 1780-1830 window (from 1808 and 1751 respectively).
- **Where held:** Ancestry (subscription) and the free auswanderer-bw.de southwestern-Germany emigration database.
- **Content note:** As with passenger/emigration lists generally, check full family entries — children are listed alongside parents.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Steuerlisten/Steuerrollen (tax lists) and Amtsrechnungen (administrative accounts), paid twice yearly; used by researchers to track household heads and widow/remarriage transitions (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Date range:** volume_search's summary lists 100 "Tax" group volumes matching Württemberg 1780-1830, all browse-only; specific date spans not broken out.
- **Where held:** Local/state archives; not further specified by a tool result for this place.
- **Substitute value:** Useful substitute for missing census and as a cross-check on name-spelling variants per the Wiki's name-spelling research-tip.

### Other record types
- **Confirmation records (Konfirmationen):** 1,065 volumes matched by volume_search for this place/period, 493 browse-only; a useful supplement when baptism entries are missing or ambiguous between same-named siblings.
- **Genealogies/compiled lineage books:** 189 "Genealogies" group volumes matched (175 browse-only), including local Ortssippenbücher (parish lineage books) and town histories (e.g. catalog_search hits like "1000 Jahre Heutingsheim" and similar Jahre-titled local histories) that sometimes reprint or index early church-book entries no longer legible in the originals.
- **Government/administrative records:** 1,304 volumes matched (705 browse-only) in that group for this place/period.

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch Historical Records | "Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971" (id 3015626, 212,026,468 persons); "Germany, Württemberg, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1818-1915" (id 4132030, 64,917 persons) | Baptism/marriage/burial coverage for this period | not stated |
| Archion | Württemberg Evangelical church records, held by the Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart (https://www.archion.de/de/archive-in-archion/baden-wuerttemberg/landeskirchliches-archiv-stuttgart/) | Direct digitized originals of the Lutheran parish registers | subscription ($) |
| Ancestry | "Württemberg, Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1985" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61023) | Baptism/marriage/burial coverage, alternate index | subscription ($) |

| GenWiki / Portal:Württemberg | http://wiki-de.genealogy.net/Portal:W%C3%BCrttemberg | General Württemberg research orientation and local finding aids | not stated |

**Coverage of this survey:** 16,120 digitized volumes match Württemberg for 1780-1830 in volume_search; only the first 10 were examined in detail (a nextPageToken was returned for further pages, not retrieved in this pass). The by-record-type summary above counts all 16,120, but individual volume titles/places beyond the first 10 were not reviewed.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Landeskirchliches Archiv Stuttgart | Original Württemberg Evangelical (Lutheran) church records | Via Archion online, or by direct correspondence/visit |

This survey named no other physical repository beyond the one above with a tool-confirmed holding.

## Records NOT online
- Many of the 16,120 matched volumes (the majority of Religious/Baptism/Religious Marriage/Religious Death groups per the volume_summary) are browse-only digitized images with no name index, meaning the images exist online but cannot be searched by name — they must be paged through image by image.

## Jurisdiction Overview
In 1812, this village lay in the Duchy of Carniola under the Habsburg monarchy. Record-keeping ran through the Catholic parish system — there was no civil marriage registration at that time.

## The Record You're Looking For
An 1812 marriage in Javorje would appear in a **Catholic parish marriage register** (matična knjiga porok). These were kept in a standard tabular format mandated by the Catholic Church, reorganized under Emperor Joseph II in the 1780s.

## Where to Search

### Online First — Matricula Online
**[Matricula Online – Slovenia](https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/slovenia/)** hosts digitized Slovenian parish-register images for free. Search for the parish that served Javorje; the town of **Škofja Loka** had its own parish and is the most likely starting point. This is your best first step.

### Physical Archive (if not online)
Per the FamilySearch Wiki, original parish registers from before the 1880s are held in archdiocesan archives, not at local parishes. The two relevant repositories are:

| Archive | Contact |
|---|---|

| **Nadškofijski arhiv Maribor**, Slomskov trg 20, SI‑2000 Maribor | skofijski.arhiv@nadskofija-maribor.si |

---

For 1820–1850, this means town-level records throughout, plus state-level registration from 1841 onward.
- **Marriage intentions** were commonly recorded in the **bride's home town**, with possible additional recordings in the groom's town and the couple's residence.

- No Berkshire County–specific probate index was confirmed by this survey; this statewide collection is the best online starting point.

The locality research guide has been saved to the project. Here's a summary of what was produced:

**Guide ID:** `loc_001` — Jalisco, Mexico, 1880–1920

**Key findings for your research:**

- **Dual record systems:** Both Catholic Church records and civil registration records (started nationally after Mexico's 1857 Reform Laws) exist for this period. For 1880–1920 Jalisco, checking *both* sources is worthwhile, as the same birth or marriage may appear in each.

- **Two-surname naming:** Mexican naming conventions use a *paternal* surname followed by a *maternal* surname (e.g., Juan García López). Online indexes typically file records under the father's (paternal) surname only, so you'll need to search both surnames and expect the maternal line surname to appear in the record body rather than the index.

- **Women's surnames:** Married women retain their birth surname in all records — they do not take their husband's name — which helps trace the maternal line.

- **Indexing gaps:** A large portion of Jalisco civil and church registers are digitized on FamilySearch and Ancestry but are **not name-indexed** and must be browsed image by image. Plan for image browsing in addition to name searches.

**Recommended next step:** Build a research plan from this guide to target the specific civil registration and Catholic church record collections identified for the family's two surnames in Jalisco.
